article_title: Under-16s could be banned from buying energy drinks in Wales

tasks.prompt: What is the article mainly about?
options: A plan to replace all soft drinks with coffee in Welsh schools
The proposed Welsh ban on selling high-caffeine energy drinks to under-16s and the debate around it
A study proving that every teenager drinks too much caffeine
New advertising rules for tea and low-caffeine cola
tasks.correct_answer: The proposed Welsh ban on selling high-caffeine energy drinks to under-16s and the debate around it
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה עוסקת בהצעת ממשלת וויילס לאסור מכירת משקאות אנרגיה עתירי קפאין לבני פחות מ־16 ובטיעונים בעד ונגד.

tasks.prompt: Which drinks would the Welsh proposal cover?
options: Every drink containing any sugar
Tea, coffee and all diet drinks
Drinks other than tea or coffee containing more than 150mg of caffeine per litre
Only drinks sold from vending machines
tasks.correct_answer: Drinks other than tea or coffee containing more than 150mg of caffeine per litre
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ההצעה מתייחסת למשקאות שאינם תה או קפה ובהם יותר מ־150 מ״ג קפאין לליטר.

tasks.prompt: What did Aisling Pigott mean when she said the ban would not be a “magic bullet”?
options: It would be too expensive to enforce.
It would work only in pharmacies.
It would immediately remove caffeine from every shop.
It would be helpful but would not solve all diet and lifestyle problems by itself.
tasks.correct_answer: It would be helpful but would not solve all diet and lifestyle problems by itself.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: Magic bullet הוא פתרון יחיד שפותר בעיה מורכבת לחלוטין; פיגוט אמרה שהאיסור הוא צעד חיובי אך לא פתרון מלא.

tasks.prompt: Which effects did the article link to excessive caffeine consumption?
options: Headaches, sleep problems and, at very high levels, heart problems or seizures
Stronger teeth and longer sleep
Permanent protection from anxiety
Improved nutrition without eating food
tasks.correct_answer: Headaches, sleep problems and, at very high levels, heart problems or seizures
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה קושרת צריכת קפאין מופרזת לכאבי ראש ולבעיות שינה, ובמקרים חמורים לדופק מהיר, הפרעות קצב או פרכוסים.

tasks.prompt: What is one issue the planned consultation will examine?
options: Whether coffee should be renamed
Online age-verification and how compliance and sanctions would work
How to remove caffeine from natural tea leaves
Whether adults should be limited to one drink a week
tasks.correct_answer: Online age-verification and how compliance and sanctions would work
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ההתייעצות אמורה לבחון בין היתר אימות גיל באינטרנט, בדיקת ציות, סנקציות, לוחות זמנים ומעקב.

tasks.prompt: Why does the British Soft Drinks Association oppose the proposed ban?
options: It wants labels removed from all drinks.
It says children should replace meals with energy drinks.
It argues the ban is unnecessary, evidence of harm is not robust, and most youth caffeine comes from other sources.
It believes the age limit should be 21.
tasks.correct_answer: It argues the ban is unnecessary, evidence of harm is not robust, and most youth caffeine comes from other sources.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הארגון טוען שאין ראיות חזקות לצריכת יתר או לנזק המצדיקים איסור, ושמרבית הקפאין של צעירים מגיע ממקורות אחרים.

tasks.prompt: Give four reasons supporters in the article offer for restricting sales to under-16s.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין ארבעה נימוקים בריאותיים או התנהגותיים הנתמכים בפרטי הכתבה.
expected_points: Young people may be more sensitive to caffeine because their bodies are smaller and their brains are developing.
High caffeine intake is associated with headaches and sleep problems.
It may contribute to stress, anxiety, irritation, tiredness or depression.
Very high intake can cause rapid heart rate, abnormal rhythms or seizures.
Sugary versions can contribute to obesity and tooth damage.
Some young people may rely on the drinks or use them instead of nutritious food.

tasks.prompt: Explain Pigott's “overdraft” comparison and how it describes the effect of caffeine.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לפרש את הדימוי ולחבר בין דחיפה זמנית בריכוז לבין ה׳החזר׳ או הנפילה שאחריה.
expected_points: An overdraft gives someone money immediately that must later be repaid.
Caffeine can provide a short-term increase in energy or concentration.
The temporary benefit is followed by a crash or another cost to the body.
The comparison warns that caffeine does not replace balanced nutrition or rest.

tasks.prompt: Summarise the Welsh proposal, its health case, public support and the industry's objection in 4–5 sentences.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכלול את גיל היעד וסף הקפאין, טיעוני הבריאות, תמיכת צעירים או מומחים, וטענת התעשייה.
expected_points: Wales plans to consult on banning sales of drinks with more than 150mg of caffeine per litre to under-16s.
Supporters cite links to sleep, mental-health and physical-health problems in young people.
Young people interviewed in Cardiff and dietician Aisling Pigott supported action.
The proposal would also require decisions about age checks, enforcement, sanctions and timing.
The British Soft Drinks Association says the measure is unnecessary and not supported by robust evidence.

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced recommendation to the Welsh consultation, using evidence from both sides of the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג עמדה ברורה אך מאוזנת, להשתמש בשתי ראיות לפחות ולתת מענה מעשי ליישום או למעקב.
expected_points: State whether the proposed restriction should proceed and why.
Use evidence about possible health effects or young people's sensitivity to caffeine.
Acknowledge the industry's argument about evidence and existing voluntary marketing rules.
Address practical issues such as online age checks, compliance, sanctions or monitoring.
Suggest reviewing outcomes after implementation rather than claiming the policy will solve every problem.
